title: Programmable Microgel Degradation in Dynamic Granular Hydrogels Guides Extracellular Matrix Assembly During Tissue Repair
abstract: ABSTRACT Granular hydrogels have attracted widespread interest for wound healing applications, yet their static design, in which microstructure and void space remain fixed, contrasts with the dynamic nature of tissue repair where processes like provisional extracellular matrix (pECM) assembly, cell organization, and nascent tissue formation evolve over time. Here, this disparity is addressed by designing dynamic granular hydrogels that are modularly assembled using microgels with pre‐programmed and precise degradation rates ranging from a few days to several weeks. Microgel degradation is controlled via modulation of hydrolytic susceptibility of hyaluronic acid polymers. The biological significance of timed pore expansion in dynamic granular hydrogels is investigated in a mouse muscle crush injury model. While slow‐degrading hydrogels support a distinct spatial assembly of cell‐instructive interstitial matrix and basement membrane proteins in the expanded pore space, this pECM remodeling is adversely altered in non‐degrading or fast‐degrading hydrogels. Slow‐degrading dynamic granular hydrogels also show long‐term therapeutic benefits on muscle wound healing, evidenced by reduced fibrosis, enhanced myogenesis, and improved functional force recovery. Collectively, these striking results demonstrate the profound significance of incorporating dynamicity through controlled microgel degradation in advanced granular biomaterials to improve tissue repair outcomes.

title: Maleimide‐Functionalized Conjugated Polymers Enable Covalent Biotic–Abiotic Integration to Boost Microbial Electrosynthesis
abstract: ABSTRACT Integrating advanced conductive materials into microbial electrosynthesis systems is a powerful paradigm for merging abiotic performance with biotic specificity, facilitating sustainable transformation of organic waste and carbon dioxide into value‐added chemicals. The regulation of biotic‐abiotic hybrid interfaces in biohybrids is crucial for improving surface microbial abundance, enhancing electron injection, and increasing electrosynthesis production. Herein, maleimide‐functionalized conjugated polymers (p(mNDI‐gT2)) were employed to construct robust, covalent bio‐interfaces via in situ click reactions with cytochrome thiol groups of Shewanella oneidensis , resulting in a doubling of bacterial adhesion. Moreover, intimate contact and binding interactions drastically reduce interfacial resistance and boost electron injection. As a direct consequence of this optimized architecture, the system achieved a 23‐fold increase in electron transfer and a 6‐fold improvement in electrochemical reduction relative to bare S. oneidensis . Furthermore, it obviously outperformed the non‐covalent group, yielding a 2‐fold enhancement in total charge output and a 2‐fold increase in succinate yield. Molecular docking simulations and proteomic analysis collectively reveal that p(mNDI‐gT2) not only facilitates efficient charge transfer but also predominantly upregulates the expression of key respiratory and bio‐interface protein complexes. Fundamentally, this covalent biotic–abiotic interface transcends traditional bulk‐adsorption methods, shifting the paradigm from simple microbial coating to molecular‐level interface engineering.

title: Phenol-Driven Modulation Enables the Crystallization of Titanium Metal–Organic Frameworks
abstract: Abstract Titanium-based metal–organic frameworks (MOFs) remain among the most challenging frameworks to synthesize due to the high reactivity of Ti(IV) precursors, particularly when in combination with strongly coordinating phenolate ligands. Phenol is an untapped modulator for MOF synthesis that enabled the formation of a new crystalline Ti-MOF phase, otherwise unattainable through established modulators. We show how transient Ti-phenolate species formed in solution regulate titanium coordination equilibria and demonstrate the broader applicability of phenol modulation for several reported Ti-MOF systems. As a result of phenol modulation, we isolate a previously elusive crystalline titanium ellagate sustainable MOF, TUW-11, composed of monometallic Ti(IV) centers and plant-derived ellagic acid linkers. Three-dimensional electron diffraction, synchrotron X-ray techniques, and scanning transmission electron microscopy reveal a layered microporous framework with 1.1 nm channels. TUW-11 exhibits a narrow band gap, p-type semiconducting behavior, and ligand-centered visible-light photoresponse. These findings demonstrate phenol modulation as a powerful strategy for controlling titanium-phenolate framework formation and expand the synthetic toolbox available for Ti-MOF discovery.

title: Modulating Bonding States and Stability of Conductive Coordination Polymers
abstract: ABSTRACT Conductive coordination polymers (CCPs) could combine the merits of both conductive polymers and metal‐organic frameworks (MOFs) and hence have attracted extensive attention for various applications. However, the modulation of their properties is challenging and rarely studied. Herein, three CCPs, denoted as Cu─6O, Cu─6N, and Cu─3O3N, featuring Cu─O 4 , Cu─(NH) 4 , and Cu─O 2 (NH) 2 units respectively, are constructed to systematically investigate the effect of the ligating atoms and bonding states on the properties. Spectroscopic and theoretical analyses reveal that Cu─O bonds are dominated by electrostatic interactions, whereas Cu─N bonds exhibit stronger covalent character, and the mixed Cu─O 2 (NH) 2 unit further enhances the overall bond strength by optimizing orbital hybridization and energy matching. Consequently, Cu─6O shows the weakest Cu─X (X═O or NH) bonds, poorest thermal stability and undergoes irreversible degradation upon base conditions at pH above ∼9.5, while also suffering severe structural degradation under electrochemical condition. The degradation mechanism was also revealed. Conversely, the stronger coordination bonds in Cu─6N and Cu─3O3N endow them with superior thermal, chemical, and electrochemical stability. This work highlights the essential role of ligating atoms in determining the bonding states and provides a design principle for developing robust CCPs.

title: Construction of Single-Atom Cobalt in Ordered Mesoporous Metal–Organic Frameworks for Boosting CO2 Conversion
abstract: Abstract Constructing single-atom transition-metal-implanted mesoporous metal–organic frameworks (MOFs) for CO2 conversion is of great importance for achieving carbon neutrality, yet remains a formidable challenge. This work presents a modular optimization of cerium-based metal–organic frameworks by incorporating Co single atoms with ordered mesopores (OMCU). These periodically arranged mesopores in OMCU were fabricated by synergistically combining the Hofmeister effect with a soft-template structure-oriented strategy. Mechanistic investigations reveal that the Co single atoms could not only accelerate photogenerated electron participation in CO2 conversion but also lower the energy barrier by promoting the formation of a new intermediate, *OCHO, along a specific reduction pathway, as directly observed by in situ Raman and operando ATR-IR spectroscopy. Density functional theory calculations corroborate that Co atoms favor the generation of *OCHO-related intermediates, omitting the high energy input for CO2·– formation and resulting in outstanding CO2 reduction performance, which is equivalent to a 10.84-fold enhancement in CO generation rate compared to that of the pristine MOF in the presence of TEA and bipyridinium ruthenium. This work provides an effective strategy through the construction of active cobalt sites within ordered mesoporous cerium-based MOFs for modulating the key intermediates in CO2 photoreduction.

title: Hydrogen-bond-mediated quasi-two-dimensional covalent organic frameworks for ultrahigh gold extraction
abstract: Covalent organic frameworks (COFs) are ideal for precious metal recovery due to their high surface areas and tunable binding sites. However, the confinement of binding sites within inner pores often leads to restricted mass transfer, resulting in poor site accessibility and limited extraction capacities. Herein, we report a quasi-two-dimensional (quasi-2D) topology-directed strategy to construct exposed binding sites for highly efficient gold recovery. By incorporating outward-pointing hydroxyl groups, the local conformation of the imine-linked skeleton is effectively locked via inter-chain hydrogen bonding (ICHB), which suppresses molecular torsion and promotes ordered assembly of the 1D chains into a quasi-2D crystalline architecture. This structural rigidification creates unobstructed ion-diffusion pathways and maximizes the exposure of active sites for rapid [AuCl4]− capture and reduction. Remarkably, under mild thermal and vibratory stimulation, gold nanoparticles form in situ and aggregate, yielding a high gold extraction capacity of 5082.32 mg g−1. Theoretical calculations demonstrate that ICHB-induced structural planarization creates a cooperative coordination environment and optimizes the energetic landscape for dechlorination, synergistically promoting guest enrichment and interfacial gold reduction. This work establishes a new blueprint for creating COFs with exposed active sites via inter-chain assembly, offering a scalable approach to maximize site accessibility and electron transfer for selective gold capture. Covalent organic frameworks are ideal for precious metal recovery but the confinement of binding sites within inner pores often leads to restricted mass transfer and limits extraction capacities. Here, the authors report a quasi-2D topology-directed strategy to construct exposed binding sites for highly efficient gold recovery.

title: Dynamically and Reversibly Functionalized Self-Assembled Platelets via Noncovalent Interactions
abstract: Abstract The creation of polymeric assemblies with reconfigurable surface functionality remains a major challenge for programmable soft materials. Covalent modification strategies can provide stable functional materials, but often require harsh reaction conditions or irreversible bond formation. Here, we integrate noncovalent interactions with crystallization-driven self-assembly (CDSA) to construct polymer platelets with region-selective functionalization and controllable responsiveness under mild conditions. Polycaprolactone-based platelets bearing cyclodextrin, barbituric acid, or related recognition motifs were prepared and subsequently orthogonal modified with complementary fluorescent guests through host–guest interactions or hydrogen bonding. Confocal fluorescence microscopy confirmed platelet-localized dye incorporation, while competitive displacement and relabeling demonstrated reversible molecular loading and release without disrupting platelet structural integrity. This work establishes supramolecular modification of CDSA-based assemblies as a modular route to soft materials with controllable and reconfigurable molecular functionality under mild conditions.

title: Biocompatible mesoporous silica particles for enzyme immobilization: A review
abstract: Enzyme immobilization within mesoporous silica is a powerful strategy for improving biocatalyst stability, reusability, and process economics in industrial applications. Conventional mesoporous silica materials, such as MCM-41 and SBA-15, possess high surface area, tunable pore size, and excellent thermal stability; however, their synthesis typically relies on surfactant templates and harsh calcination procedures that are incompatible with fragile biomolecules and sustainable manufacturing. In contrast, biocompatible mesoporous silica prepared through non-surfactant templating employs mild extraction conditions compatible with one-pot enzyme immobilization and direct hydrogel coating. The properties of biocompatible mesoporous silica particles (BMSP) can be further enhanced through surface engineering using silane coupling agents, crosslinking chemistry, and silanol density enhancement to improve enzyme–support interactions and immobilization efficiency. Hybrid architectures incorporating magnetic materials, organic polymers, carbonaceous supports, metal oxides, and hierarchical pore networks further expand BMSP functionality by enabling catalyst recovery, enhanced biocompatibility, improved structural robustness, and superior mass transport. However, these engineering strategies may also introduce diffusion limitations, enzyme conformational changes, and additional material and processing burdens that can significantly affect biocatalytic performance and environmental sustainability. This review systematically examines the structure–performance relationships associated with these challenges and evaluates the environmental implications of non-surfactant synthesis, surface functionalization, and hybrid material integration. Mitigation strategies, including larger non-surfactant templates, hierarchical meso-macroporous architectures, and optimized surface functionalization, are discussed to alleviate diffusion limitations and preserve enzyme structure. Quantitative descriptors, including the Thiele modulus, effectiveness factor, Michaelis constant (Km), and maximum reaction rate (Vmax), are highlighted as engineering tools for evaluating support performance and guiding rational materials design. This review provides a framework for developing next-generation biocompatible mesoporous silica platforms for sustainable industrial biocatalysis.

title: Constructing the Transfer Ladder between Active Sites and Functional Units within the Cluster-Based Catalyst for Reductive Amination
abstract: Abstract The remote communication between active sites and the surrounding environment within a heterogeneous catalyst for the orderly bonding of reactive species is highly desired yet very challenging. Here we find that the phosphotungstate with a mesoporous framework (abbreviated as mPTA) has an extraordinary ability to accommodate ammonia but has no activity for catalytic reductive amination, while the Pd3(S-Adm)3(PPh3)3+ (Pd3 for short; S-Adm = 1-adamantanethiol) cluster enables the above reaction but insufficient ammonia occurring on the cluster leads to low activity and inferior selectivity. We thereby construct a transfer channel between the active cluster (Pd3) and the functional unit (mPTA), which is identified as an interfacial ladder of Pd–O–W, delivering ammonia molecules from the functional unit to the active center. The mPTA resembles a pump source to supply ammonia to meet the requirement for the reductive amination over the cluster, in which ammonia hops the ladder to expediently react with H2 and carbonyl compounds awaiting on Pd sites, finally giving rise to remarkable performances with a high yield of amines. We recognize that the interactive cooperation of inner catalysis with peripheral input across two different compounds holds promise in decoupling and controlling complex chemical ecosystems for high-quality productivity.

title: Hierarchical Descriptor-Driven Machine Learning Reveals the Structure–Performance Landscape of Hydrogen-Bonded Organic Frameworks for CO 2 /N 2 Separation
abstract: Abstract Hydrogen-bonded organic frameworks (HOFs) are emerging as promising adsorbents for postcombustion CO2 capture owing to their mild self-assembly, solution processability, and facile regeneration, yet the structural and chemical factors governing their separation performance remain poorly resolved. Here, we report an integrated computational workflow combining high-throughput GCMC simulation, interpretable machine learning, and atomistic mechanism analysis to evaluate 84,261 HOFs for CO2/N2 separation under simulated flue-gas conditions. After benchmarking against experimental isotherms, a hierarchical four-level descriptor set spanning geometric, thermodynamic, elemental, and chemical/electronic features was constructed. Among eight algorithms, XGBoost delivered the highest accuracy (R2 = 0.93), and both feature importance and SHAP analyses identified geometric and thermodynamic descriptors as the dominant determinants of selectivity. High-performance HOFs converge on a common signature of smaller pores, denser frameworks, and enriched polar hydrogen-bond-donating groups (amino and carboxyl moieties), which cooperatively strengthen framework-CO2 interactions and widen the CO2/N2 heat-of-adsorption gap. Three-dimensional density mapping and geometry-based hydrogen-bond statistics confirm that preferential framework-CO2 hydrogen bonding is the key microscopic driving force, whereas N2 remains uniformly dispersed and forms essentially no effective hydrogen bonds. This work provides a high-fidelity predictive model and transferable design rules that advance HOF-based CO2/N2 separation from isolated breakthroughs toward mechanism-guided systematic design.

title: Decoction-inspired thermo-mechanical coupling creates hierarchical nanohelix from herbal medicine for lipophagy therapy
abstract: Abstract Oral supramolecular nanomedicines often suffer from kinetic trapping, forming metastable aggregates with poor gastrointestinal stability and premature drug release. Conventional assembly methods rarely overcome these barriers. Inspired by the traditional Chinese medicine (TCM) decoction process, which intrinsically combines heating with mechanical stirring, we applied a thermo-mechanical coupling strategy to baicalin and berberine assemblies. Coupled thermal energy and fluid shear drove a transition from kinetically trapped metastable aggregate to thermodynamically stable left-handed nanohelix with an ordered crystalline lattice. This higher degree of structural order conferred improved gastrointestinal tolerance and extended the in vivo mean residence time to 23.06 ± 0.47 h. Sustained systemic exposure activated the AMPK–FoxO1–TFEB–lysosome axis, promoted hepatic lipophagy, and alleviated metabolic dysfunction-associated fatty liver disease in mice. These findings provide a physical chemistry framework for overcoming kinetic traps in supramolecular assembly, elucidate the nanoscale organization underlying traditional decoction, and offer a design strategy for long-acting oral nanotherapeutics.

title: Layered Precursor‐Guided Growth of Nondegenerate Amorphous In 2 O 3 Approaching the Thickness Limit
abstract: ABSTRACT Oxide semiconductors are promising channel materials for ultrathin electronics. However, conventional growth methods often produce excess carriers, poor stability, and interfacial issues, limiting their electronic applications. Here, we present a layered precursor‐guided synthesis of atom‐thin amorphous indium oxide (In 2 O 3 ) by oxidizing a layered InSe precursor within a back‐end‐of‐line (BEOL)‐compatible thermal budget. The oxide thickness is precisely controlled by the number of precursor layers, enabling In 2 O 3 as thin as 0.63 nm at the physical thickness limit. By avoiding localized nucleation and island coalescence issues, the resulting In 2 O 3 exhibits atomically smooth surfaces and excellent electrostatic uniformity with potential variations below 22 meV. Capacitance‐voltage analyses confirm a carrier density of 2.8 × 10 18 cm −3 in the nondegenerate regime and a low interface trap density of 10 10 ∼10 11 cm −2 ·eV −1 . We further demonstrate reproducible enhancement‐mode transistors with sub‐3 nm channels, featuring near‐zero threshold voltage, a low subthreshold swing (SS) of ∼74 mV/dec, a negligible hysteresis of < 10 mV, and robust gate‐stress stability. This work establishes a reliable route for integrating ultrathin, high‐performance amorphous oxide semiconductors, pushing the limits of next‐generation nanoelectronics.

title: In-cell structures visualize human pre-ribosome assembly in the nucleolus
abstract: In eukaryotes, ribosome biogenesis initiates within the nucleolus, a hallmark multilayered compartment of the nucleus. Structures of pre-ribosomes have been characterized ex situ, but their assembly pathways within human nucleoli have not been described. Here, we used cryogenic correlative light and electron tomography to visualize molecular landscapes within HeLa cell nucleoli and obtained in-cell structural snapshots of both ribosomal subunit precursors, the small subunit processome and the pre-60S. These recapitulate major states resolved previously ex situ and reveal additional critical interaction partners, including the RNA exosome, rixosome, and nuclear export receptor CRM1-RanGTP. We further show how pre-ribosome assembly landscapes are altered upon RNA polymerase I inhibition. Our study combines molecular structures with cellular context to elucidate the spatiotemporal assembly pathway of the human ribosome.

title: Stimulated protein degradation to promote mitochondrial function and neuronal survival
abstract: Targeted protein degradation is a promising modality to treat cancer or inflammation, but whether it can provide a similar benefit for disorders caused by pervasive protein dysregulation is unclear. We describe stimulated protein degradation (SPD) as a strategy that leverages agonists of stress-responsive E3 ubiquitin ligases to simultaneously eliminate multiple pathogenic factors. Specifically, we show that activators of the reductive stress response E3 CUL2 FEM1B boost degradation of multiple physiological substrates to improve mitochondrial import and electron transport chain assembly. In this manner, CUL2 FEM1B agonists preserve mitochondrial function and neuronal survival in models of neurodegenerative COX deficiency syndrome and Friedreich’s ataxia. By activating E3 ligases that evolved to safeguard cellular integrity, SPD expands the use of compound-induced protein degradation to complex pathologies of high unmet need.

title: Spatial coordination in the codevelopment of the human urogenital system during organogenesis
abstract: The human urogenital system originates from a common embryonic domain, yet the mechanisms guiding its spatiotemporal coordination remain understudied. Here, we combined high-resolution spatial transcriptomics with single-cell multiomics to profile human embryos from Carnegie stages 15 to 23, capturing the codevelopmental dynamics of the urogenital system. We revealed mesonephros- and adrenal primordium–derived signals that promote gonadal specification and enable efficient in vitro generation of cells resembling early gonadal lineages. We also uncovered a possible mesonephric origin of gonadal supporting cells through rete testis or ovarii linking the mesonephros. Finally, we delineate three transcriptionally distinct steroidogenic lineages differing in cholesterol sourcing, cortisol synthesis, and sex hormone production that together orchestrate sex differentiation. These findings deepen our understanding of urogenital system assembly and guide the exploration of coordinated multiorgan development.

title: Decentralized Biosynthesis of the Spiro-DKP Alkaloid Chevalinulin A Enabled by Nonclustered P450 and Intermolecular [4 + 2] Cyclase
abstract: Abstract Intermolecular Diels–Alder (DA) cycloadditions are pivotal for constructing complex polycyclic architectures. However, biological catalysts performing this transformation on diketopiperazine (DKP) cores remain largely unidentified. Here, we report a decentralized biosynthetic pathway in the deep-sea cold-seep sourced fungus Aspergillus chevalieri CS-122 that assembles chevalinulin A, a spiro[bicyclo[2.2.2]octane]-DKP alkaloid. This pathway involves two nonclustered enzymes, CalO and FadA. CalO is a cytochrome P450 that furnishes an essential exocyclic olefin, while FadA represents the first FAD oxidoreductase-like Diels–Alderase that catalyzes an intermolecular, endoselective [4 + 2] cycloaddition between neoechinulin B and 3,4-trans-cyclohexadiene. These enzymes function downstream of a conserved gene cluster, effectively decoupling core scaffold assembly from late-stage functionalization. This strategy likely underpins the extensive structural diversity of fungal DKP alkaloids. Notably, CalO and FadA were identified via an integrated transcriptomic and structure-guided computational pipeline, rather than sequence homology, demonstrating the efficacy of this approach in mining functional catalysts from genomic “dark matter”. Mutational analysis indicates that residues M193, Y226, Y315, and D446 are critical in FadA activity. This study reveals a decentralized biosynthetic paradigm linking clustered core assembly with dispersed diversification, establishing a general framework for engineering complex alkaloid scaffolds.

title: Conjugation of metal-organic framework (MIL-125) to NiFe2O4@CdS nanoparticles for enhanced photocatalytic hydrogen generation
abstract: Abstract Harnessing solar energy with semiconductors offers a feasible path toward sustainable hydrogen production via photocatalytic water splitting. In this study, a ternary photocatalyst, MIL-125(Ti)/NiFe 2 O 4 @CdS, was fabricated by integrating a Ti-based metal–organic framework with a green-synthesized NiFe 2 O 4 @CdS binary core–shell heterostructure for visible-light-driven hydrogen evolution. Illicium verum Hook. f. (star anise) extract was used as a natural reducing and stabilizing agent for NiFe 2 O 4 nanoparticles preparation prior to the fabrication of the binary photocatalyst. The ternary composite was comprehensively characterized by structural, morphological, optical, and photoelectrochemical techniques. Compared with the individual components, the ternary photocatalyst exhibited enhanced visible-light absorption, a reduced band gap (2.42 eV), and a mesoporous structure with a BET surface area of 148.62 m²/g, pore volume of 0.5721 cm 3 /g, and a mean pore diameter of 15.0 nm. Photoelectrochemical analyses revealed improved charge separation, the lowest charge-transfer resistance, the highest photocurrent response, the largest electrochemically active surface area, and favorable band alignment. Consequently, MIL-125/NiFe 2 O 4 @CdS achieved an initial hydrogen evolution rate of 1.62231 mmol g − 1 h − 1 and a cumulative hydrogen production of 10.20386 mmol g − 1 after 5 h, significantly outperforming CdS and the binary NiFe 2 O 4 @CdS. The photocatalyst retained approximately 60% of its initial activity after four reaction cycles, demonstrating good stability. The enhanced performance is attributed to the synergistic effects of MIL-125, which increase surface area, improve light harvesting, and promote efficient charge separation and transfer through a dual direct Z-scheme heterojunction. These findings highlight MIL-125/NiFe 2 O 4 @CdS as a promising photocatalyst for sustainable hydrogen production.

title: Framework Deuteration Regulates Excited-State Dynamics and H2O2 Release in Covalent Organic Framework Photocatalysis
abstract: Abstract Hydrogen/deuterium (H/D) substitution provides a unique means of perturbing nuclear motion while largely preserving electronic structure. Here, we investigate isotope-regulated photocatalysis using structurally matched H-TpPa and D-TpPa covalent organic frameworks (COFs) for H2O2 production. Deuteration preserves framework connectivity, crystallinity, porosity, and ground-state electronic structure, yet increases the H2O2 production rate by 1.80-fold in O2-saturated pure water. Spectroscopic and theoretical analyses show that D-TpPa exhibits weaker effective exciton–phonon coupling, a lower apparent exciton-dissociation energy, a longer-lived photoexcited population, and redistributed mode-resolved Huang–Rhys contributions, collectively improving charge utilization. Both isotopologues follow the same coupled two-electron oxygen reduction and four-electron water oxidation pathway. At the catalytic interface, isotope-dependent vibrational free-energy contributions reduce terminal *HOOH stabilization and lower the free-energy requirement for H2O2 release. These results establish framework isotope engineering as a generic strategy for regulating photocatalysis from excited-state evolution to interfacial product release without substantial electronic reconstruction.

title: Interweaving Two‐Dimensional Co‐Corrole‐Based Covalent Organic Framework for Significantly Improved Electrocatalytic Oxygen Reduction Reaction
abstract: ABSTRACT Two‐dimensional (2D) covalent organic frameworks (COFs) are promising electrocatalysts but suffer from limited active‐site accessibility, sluggish mass transportation in narrow‐spaced interlayers, and interlayer sliding during catalysis. Herein, we report the synthesis of Co‐corrole‐based 2D COF 1 and its interlayer‐interweaved derivatives 2 and 3 for electrocatalytic oxygen reduction reaction (ORR). The reaction of Co tris(4‐formylphenyl)corrole and 1,4‐phenylenediamine gave 2D COF 1 with an interlayer spacing of 4.2 Å. Using pyrazine and bipyridine as bidentate molecular pillars to interweave 2D layers of 1 via bridging interlayer Co corroles, we obtained COFs 2 and 3 with interlayer spacing of 6.4 and 10.3 Å, respectively. Structural and spectroscopic analyses confirmed that the expanded interlayer spacing is caused by the axial Co–N coordination between Co corroles and bidentate molecular pillars. Compared to 1 , COFs 2 and 3 exhibited markedly enhanced 4H + /4e – ORR activity and durability, with half‐wave potential increased from 0.80 to 0.89 V and 0.94 V versus RHE. Rotation‐rate‐dependent Tafel measurements revealed improved mass transportation in the enlarged interlayer spaces in 2 and 3 . The Zn‐air battery using COF 3 delivered a high open‐circuit voltage of 1.52 V and a large peak power density of 193.5 Mw cm −2 , outperforming Pt/Ru benchmarks.

title: Hierarchical Copper-Based Metal-Organic Frameworks for Improved Catalytic Performance
abstract: Introducing additional meso- or macroporosity into traditionally microporous metal-organic frameworks (MOFs) can greatly improve the catalytic performance of these materials, by reducing diffusional barriers during reactions. In this study, we demonstrate that HKUST-1 synthesized via supercritical CO2-assisted crystallization (referred to here as “scCO2-HKUST”) forms a hierarchically porous structure, combining intrinsic microporosity with newly formed macropores. X-ray diffraction (PXRD), scanning electron microscopy (SEM), and gas sorption analyses confirmed the preservation of the crystal structure alongside macropore formation. X-ray photoelectron spectroscopy (XPS) revealed a higher proportion of low-valent copper species (Cuo/Cu+) in scCO₂-HKUST compared to conventional HKUST-1, indicative of increased coordinatively unsaturated metal sites. In catalytic CO oxidation, scCO2-HKUST achieved higher conversion rates than normal HKUST-1 between 220 and 260 oC, with complete CO conversion at 260 °C versus 280 °C for the conventional sample. This enhanced activity is attributed to faster molecular diffusion through the macropores and greater accessibility of reactive copper sites.

title: High-order nanofluidic spiking encoding
abstract: Abstract High-order memristor is needed in neuromorphic engineering for sophisticated neural encoding. Progress has been made in solid-state memristor with electronic dynamics, which, however, presents a significant disparity with the ionic-chemical signaling in the human brain. Herein, we realize high-order nanofluidic spiking encoding based on synergizing the high porosity for non-linear ion transport, light responsibility for optical sensing, and catalytic chemistry for biological perception of a multifunctional covalent organic framework under nanoconfinement. The unique multimodal responses make possible the co-encoded spiking by electricity, light and real neurotransmitter glutamate in the physiological media, leading to the significantly enriched synaptic plasticity towards high-order spiking encoding behaviors, i.e. the rate encoding, time-to-first-spike encoding, rate and temporal fusion encoding, and history-dependent spiking encoding. It is expected to be a starting point for high-order nanofluidic spiking encoding.

title: Disentangling protein confinement from surface adsorption in hierarchical zirconium metal-organic frameworks
abstract: A persistent challenge in protein immobilization within metal-organic frameworks (MOFs) is distinguishing genuine internal confinement from surface adsorption and interparticle voids, which can mimic encapsulation despite fundamentally different spatial microenvironments. Incorporating mesochannels to produce hierarchical UiO-66-NH 2 and MOF-808 nanoparticles, prepared by micelle templating, offers a strategy to overcome this ambiguity while preserving their intrinsic microporosity. Evidence from pore accessibility, pulsed field gradient NMR, and small-angle X-ray scattering is consistent with protein association within mesochannel environments. In the hierarchical hosts, loaded bovine serum albumin shows enhanced resilience to thermal stress. Together, these results are consistent with internal mesochannel confinement contributing to protein stabilization while preserving molecular accessibility in MOFs. Extending confinement to function, Candida antarctica lipase B immobilized in these hosts remains catalytically active at elevated temperature. In contrast to a commercial immobilized preparation, it retains a larger fraction of its activity in the first reuse cycles.

title: Fluoride-Enabled Assembly of Iron–Hydrogen-Bonded Frameworks as Bifunctional Lewis Acid–Base Catalysts for Knoevenagel Condensation
abstract: Abstract The development of recyclable heterogeneous catalysts that enable efficient organic transformations without solvents is important for sustainable chemical synthesis. In this work, two new fluoride-mediated metal–hydrogen-bonded organic frameworks (M-HOFs), labeled as JOU-40 and JOU-41, were successfully synthesized. Single-crystal X-ray diffraction reveals that both M-HOFs feature [Fe3F11]n chains that are extended into three-dimensional supramolecular networks through O–H···F hydrogen bonds. The resulting frameworks integrate Lewis-acidic iron centers and basic fluoride sites within a confined porous environment, enabling efficient Lewis acid–base catalysis. As heterogeneous catalysts, JOU-40 and JOU-41 efficiently promote the solvent-free Knoevenagel condensation of benzaldehyde with malononitrile, affording >99.00% conversion and selectivity. The catalyst also exhibits good substrate compatibility across a range of substituted aldehydes. More fascinatingly, kinetic analyses reveal that the reaction can be described by the Avrami nucleation–growth model, highlighting the coupled contributions of chemical conversion and product crystallization. Density functional theory (DFT) calculations demonstrate that the adjacent Fe3+ and F– sites activate the two reactants and facilitate C═C bond formation, providing a molecular-level basis for the observed catalytic activity. This work offers new design insights for developing highly efficient, stable, and recyclable catalytic systems for solvent-free Knoevenagel condensation.

title: pH-Responsive Self-Assembly and Reversible Rheology of a Single-Component Amine Oxide Surfactant-Based Fracturing Fluid
abstract: Abstract To address the insufficient thermal stability, poor recyclability, and formulation complexity of conventional viscoelastic surfactant (VES) fracturing fluids under the high-temperature and strongly stress-sensitive conditions of deep coalbed methane (CBM) reservoirs, a single-component zwitterionic amine oxide surfactant, N,N-dimethyl-4-(tetradecyloxy)benzylamine oxide (P-ToDo), was developed as a pH-responsive VES fracturing fluid. The structure–performance relationship and pH-responsive thickening mechanism of P-ToDo were systematically evaluated through rheological measurements, pH-switching tests, coal core permeability experiments, and molecular dynamics (MD) simulations. The rigid benzene ring in P-ToDo contributed to enhanced thermal and shear resistance, while the amine oxide headgroup enabled protonation-regulated pH-responsive behavior and reversible viscosity control. Rheological results showed that the single-component 3 wt % P-ToDo system exhibited excellent thickening performance near neutral pH, maintaining an apparent viscosity of 34.54 mPa s after shearing at 120 °C and 170 s–1 for 1 h. Upon adjustment of the pH between 7.53 and 9.00, the system underwent reversible switching between a high-viscosity fracturing state and a low-viscosity gel-breaking state, indicating good recyclability. In addition, coal core permeability tests showed a low average damage rate of 10.85%. MD simulations further revealed that the protonation degree modulated intermolecular nonbonded interactions and aggregate compactness, thereby explaining the experimentally observed pH-responsive rheological behavior. These findings establish P-ToDo as a reusable, single-component VES platform that integrates pH-triggered rheological regulation, robust high-temperature performance, and simplified fluid formulation, offering a sustainable strategy for efficient fracturing stimulation in deep CBM reservoirs.

title: Programming Closed Pores in Hard Carbon Anodes via Alcohol‐Regulated Interfacial Assembly for High‐Rate and Durable Sodium‐Ion Storage
abstract: ABSTRACT Closed pores are widely recognized as the primary structural domains responsible for the low‐voltage plateau capacity of hard carbon anodes for sodium‐ion batteries (SIBs). However, current strategies for constructing closed pores predominantly rely on post‐carbonization reconstruction, offering limited control over pore accessibility and interfacial chemistry. Here we demonstrate that closed pores can instead be programmed during the precursor assembly process via an alcohol‐regulated interfacial assembly strategy. By systematically modulating the alcohol/water solvent environment, hydrogen‐bond interactions, micelle swelling behavior, and pyrrole polymerization kinetics are cooperatively regulated, enabling programmable precursor confinement and the subsequent transformation of micelle‐pyrrole assemblies into closed‐pore‐rich hard carbons during carbonization. The optimized hard carbon exhibits abundant closed ultramicropores that not only facilitate the quasi‐metallic sodium cluster filling but also promote the formation of a thin inorganic‐rich solid electrolyte interphase (SEI) layer, thereby accelerating sodium‐storage kinetics. As a result, it delivers an outstanding rate capability of 119 mAh g −1 at 10 A g −1 and robust cycling stability over 6000 cycles at 5 A g −1 , as well as excellent low‐temperature performance at −20°C. This work establishes precursor organization programming as a general strategy for constructing closed pores in hard carbon materials toward fast‐charging and long‐life SIBs.

title: Framework-Templated Single Clathrate Hydrate Cages in Metal–Organic Frameworks
abstract: Molecular simulations identify metal–organic framework (MOF) pores that retain single methane hydrate cages and, for a nonstandard 16-water cage, support its assembly from disordered water. In smooth spherical pores, a methane molecule assembled twenty waters into the pentagonal dodecahedron of structure I hydrate and sixteen waters into a 435661 cage, a polyhedron that no known hydrate crystal contains. These idealized models were built by language-model agents and then walked back toward real materials, an approach referred to here as agentic doodling, and they guided a screening of 120,419 experimental MOF structures. Most size-matched pores pulled the cage apart, but a small set of frameworks kept it intact at 216 K, better with methane than without, and ELOZIQ kept the dodecahedron up to 270 K, near the melting temperature of the water model. In XODDED and GUQMAH, the nonstandard cage was held at least as well as in an ideal spherical pore, and it self-assembled around methane from randomly placed water, with nearly all of its edges hydrogen bonded. The pores template the cages through a moderate attraction spread over the cage corners rather than through strong binding sites placed at the corners. These results open a route to designing MOFs that hold single hydrate cages, including cages that do not occur in bulk hydrates.

title: Crystal Integrity Suppresses Bulk Trapping in Potassium Poly(Heptazine Imide) for Selective Polyester Photoreforming
abstract: ABSTRACT Bulk defects in organic semiconductor photocatalysts intercept photogenerated charges before interfacial reaction, constraining activity and selectivity. Here, seeded molten‐salt recrystallization yields potassium poly(heptazine imide) (PHI‐K) nanocrystals with reduced cyano content and enhanced lattice coherence for polyester photoreforming. Density functional theory and transient absorption spectroscopy identify cyano‐derived occupied states as bulk hole traps. Defect suppression preserves observable hole‐polaron absorption and extends the average exciton‐associated absorption decay time from 69.52 to 984.72 ps, consistent with reduced trap‐assisted carrier loss. Under air mass 1.5 global (AM 1.5G) irradiation, crystalline PHI‐K photoreforms alkaline‐pretreated poly(glycolic acid) and poly(lactic acid) into glyoxylic and pyruvic acids with respective target‐product carbon yields of 95.2% and 92.5%. Corresponding H 2 evolution rates reach 42.6 and 26.0 mmol g −1 h −1 , with apparent quantum yields of 50.8% and 30.1% at 400 nm, respectively. In situ infrared spectroscopy, isotope effects, and carrier kinetics support a pathway in which holes drive two‐electron oxidation of surface‐bound α‐hydroxy species while electrons reduce protons on Pt. These findings establish crystal integrity as an organic semiconductor materials principle that couples bulk charge retention to selective bond conversion in conjugated photocatalysts.

title: Waveguided, Self‐Sensing Sheath–Core Liquid Crystal Elastomer Fiber Actuators
abstract: ABSTRACT Soft actuators capable of operating in confined and hard‐to‐access environments, while providing integrated self‐sensing capabilities, are highly desired for next‐generation robotic systems. Here we report a waveguided sheath‐core optical fiber actuator consisting of a liquid crystal elastomer core encased in a conductive sheath of carbon nanotubes/carbon black. Near‐infrared light guided through the fiber actuator drives reversible contractions of up to 38% and enables a load‐bearing capacity of up to 320 times the actuator's own weight. Arrays of these fibers enable independent optical addressing of individual actuators, allowing programmable multimodal gripping in confined environments. The conductive sheath simultaneously serves as a strain sensor, providing real‐time monitoring of actuation states via changes in resistance. By integrating photothermal actuation and self‐sensing into a single fiber architecture, this work establishes a multifunctional platform for soft robotic systems operating in spatially confined environments.

title: Where Ions Meet Electrons: Advanced Bioelectronic Interfaces With Organic Electrochemical Transistors
abstract: ABSTRACT Organic electrochemical transistors (OECTs) have evolved from passive electrodes into active transducers that sense, amplify, and increasingly compute at the boundary between circuits and living tissue. Over the past decade, advances span molecular design of organic mixed ionic–electronic conductors (OMIECs), electrolyte and channel engineering, device architectures, and circuit integration, to system‐level translation. Unlike existing reviews that treat these in isolation, emphasizing single material classes, mechanisms, or applications, this article unifies them through bioelectronic interface design, working from biological demands to demonstrated capabilities. We analyze operating principles, benchmarking metrics and structure–property relationships across p‐type, n‐type, and biodegradable OMIECs. The electrolyte‐channel region emerges as where biology and electronics converge; we survey gel electrolytes, semiconducting hydrogels, and all‐gel devices, alongside planar, vertical, fiber, textile, and printed architectures. We assess how design choices impact performance across electrophysiological, biochemical, implantable, wearable, and plant‐bioelectronic applications, while addressing biocompatibility, stability, and standardization requirements. Finally, we outline OECT‐native platforms that consolidate sensing, memory, computation, and actuation within closed‐loop, autonomous bioelectronic interfaces, arguing that this convergence represents the most consequential near‐term direction for the field.

title: Interfacially Stitched Bilayer Anodes Enforce Surface-Confined Hydroxyl Radical Chemistry in Complex Wastewater
abstract: Abstract Electro-oxidation technology holds great promise for wastewater treatment, yet its practical application remains hindered by insufficient selectivity in oxidative species generation and limited electrode stability under harsh operating conditions. Here, we devise a layer-by-layer anion–cation engineering strategy to fabricate an Sb–F-stitched SnO2 bilayer anode (SF–SnO2 BA), in which a fluorine-regulated SnO2 catalytic layer is interfacially anchored onto a dense Sb–SnO2 interlayer coated on a Ti foam scaffold. This hierarchically stitched architecture simultaneously modulates interfacial charge transport and stabilizes the catalytic layer, leading to markedly enhanced electrocatalytic oxidation performance across a broad pH range (1–11). When integrated into a scalable flow-through electro-oxidation system, SF–SnO2 BA enabled highly efficient mineralization (&gt;80%) of four representative industrial wastewaters at low energy consumption. Furthermore, the system also demonstrated remarkable operational durability, sustaining high mineralization efficiency (60–80%) over 14 consecutive days during continuous treatment of real aniline wastewater from a coal chemical plant. In situ spectroscopic investigations coupled with theoretical calculations collectively elucidated that water molecules are initially oxidized on the SF–SnO2 BA surface to form Sn–OH intermediates, which are subsequently transformed into Sn–O species at elevated potentials. Notably, the cooperative F···Sn–O* structural motif directs the generation of surface-confined •OH, which acts as the dominant oxidative species for pollutant degradation. This interfacially stitched bilayer anode offers a viable route toward green and sustainable electrochemical oxidation technologies for practical wastewater treatment.

title: An Air- and Moisture-Stable Fulvalene Radical Cation in a Reversible Three-State Redox Interconversion
abstract: Abstract Pentafulvalene has attracted considerable interest owing to its unique cross-conjugated electronic structure, but its intrinsic instability has limited detailed studies of its redox chemistry, particularly with respect to accessing and characterizing its radical form. Herein, we report an imidazolium-substituted zwitterionic fulvalene (IZFv) that undergoes reversible interconversion among three isolable redox states, including a fulvalene radical cation. Single-crystal X-ray diffraction, spectroscopy, and complementary NICS, HOMA, and AICD analyses reveal systematic oxidation-state-dependent changes in the structure and local aromaticity of the fulvalene framework. Notably, the dication (IZFv2+) shows the closest bond-metric and aromaticity correspondence to parent pentafulvalene (Fv) while remaining isolable and amenable to handling under ambient conditions. The radical cation (IZFv•+) is stable toward air and moisture (t1/2 = 15.2 days), exhibits a distonic electronic structure in which the unpaired spin resides predominantly on the fulvalene core while the positive charge is accommodated primarily by the imidazolium-derived carbon centers, and shows red photoluminescence at 650 nm. To the best of our knowledge, this work provides the first isolation of an oxidatively generated radical cation based on a sulfur-free, unannulated pentafulvalene scaffold and establishes an experimentally accessible platform for examining redox-dependent structural and electronic evolution within the fulvalene π-framework.

title: Rational Construction of Flexible-Rigid β-Cyclodextrin Cross-Linked Porous Microspheres for High-Efficiency Oil Absorption
abstract: Abstract Oil spills and toxic organic solvent leakage damage aquatic environments and human health, while traditional polymer oil adsorbents feature disconnected pores, weak recyclability, and conflicting adsorption capacity and structural stability. Herein, renewable β-cyclodextrin (β-CD) was esterified into a multivinyl cross-linker (β-CD-A), and flexible-rigid balanced porous DBP microspheres were synthesized via one-pot suspension copolymerization. Gradient monomer screening identified 35 mol % rigid comonomer 4-tert-butylstyrene (PTBS) as the optimal dosage. Dodecane served as a porogen to build interconnected hierarchical macro/meso/micropores, endowing DBP with high adsorption capacities of 135.6, 128.8, and 115.1 g g–1 for CCl4, CHCl3, and toluene. Adsorption obeys pseudo-first-order kinetics, driven by capillary force and van der Waals force. After 10 adsorption–desorption cycles, the microspheres reserve over 75% initial capacity, perform steadily from −20 to 60 °C, and lose less than 6% mass in water, concentrated acid, and alkali. This work demonstrates a flexible-rigid synergistic approach for fabricating hierarchically porous β-CD adsorbents. The scalable material shows potential for marine oil spill remediation and industrial organic wastewater treatment.

title: Direct Synthesis of CdSe Quantum Dot Inks in Polar Solvents with Conductive Ligands
abstract: Colloidal quantum dots (QDs) have unlocked advancements in technologies like displays and light detectors, thanks to their tuneable photoelectronic properties and scalability. However, several device schemes based on electronically conducting QD layers, such as photodetectors and LEDs, require processing QDs as concentrated inks with short, conductive ligands. Currently, this is only achievable after replacing the insulating ligands used during their colloidal synthesis, a process that is both time-consuming and resource-intensive. Direct synthesis of QD inks with short ligands remains underdeveloped in non-aqueous medium, yet such straightforward synthesis route would immensely facilitate QD device integration. In this study, we focus on cadmium selenide (CdSe), a well-understood QD system with established syntheses and surface chemistry, to showcase a strategy for directly synthesising inks with conductive ligands. We report a one-step synthesis of inorganic-passivated 3.4 nm wurtzite CdSe QDs in polar aprotic solvents. Our findings reveal a non-classical nucleation pathway with 1.5 nm magic-size clusters as intermediates. We demonstrate that highly Lewis-basic solvents and weakly coordinating cadmium counteranions are essential for producing high-quality CdSe QDs, particularly with hexamethylphosphoramide as a solvent and tetrafluoroborate counteranions for cadmium. Surface characterisations, including solid-state NMR, Raman, and IR spectroscopy, and ζ-potential measurements, reveal a disordered QD surface rich in cadmium-oxygen bonds and phosphates, which quenches the photoluminescence.

title: Highly Ordered Flexible Fibrous Membrane Electrode With Pt Nanoparticles Supported on Fe‐Containing N‐Doped Carbon for Oxygen Reduction Reaction
abstract: ABSTRACT Pt nanoparticles supported on porous carbon supports are widely used as electrocatalysts in proton exchange membrane fuel cells (PEMFCs), but conventional carbon supports suffer from corrosion and Pt agglomeration, which limit performance and durability. Herein, we address these issues by anchoring Pt nanoparticles on highly ordered Fe‐containing N‐doped carbon nanofibers (Pt‐FeNC). Owing to the flexible, ordered fibrous‐membrane architecture and an interfacial electronic interaction between Pt and the Fe─N─C support, charge transport and improves catalyst durability. As a result, Pt‐FeNC exhibits high oxygen reduction reaction (ORR) activity, with a half‐wave potential of 0.9 V. A membrane electrode assembly (MEA) employing the ordered fibrous membrane as a freestanding cathode delivers an approximately 33% higher peak power density than commercial Pt/C and only a 7.2% performance loss after 30,000 accelerated stress test cycles. The enhanced performance is attributed to the improved durability of the Fe‐containing N‐doped carbon support and the continuous electron‐ and mass‐transport pathways provided by the interconnected fibrous network.

title: Chiral Carbon Dots‐Triggered Conjugated Polymer Assembly for Efficient Circularly Polarized Electroluminescence and Photodetection †
abstract: Comprehensive Summary The integration of circularly polarized organic light‐emitting diodes (CP‐OLEDs) and circularly polarized light (CPL) photodetectors into a unified chiral material platform represents a critical step toward advanced optoelectronics, yet achieving high performance in both devices remains a formidable challenge. Here, we demonstrate a chiral emissive material engineered through helical co‐assembly of an achiral conjugated polymer, poly(9,9‐dioctylfluorene‐ co ‐benzothiadiazole) (F8BT), with nano‐scaled chiral carbon dots (C‐dots). Owing to efficient chirality and energy transfer from chiral C‐dots to F8BT, the composite films demonstrate strong optical activity and CPL properties, which are further simultaneously used as chiral active layers for constructing high‐performance CP‐OLEDs and CPL photodetectors. Notably, the resulting CP‐OLEDs show a maximum electroluminescence dissymmetry factor (| g EL |) of 9.4 × 10 −3 , high luminance of 18372 cd·m −2 and unprecedented operational stability with half lifetime of 22908 h at an initial luminance of 100 cd·m −2 . Moreover, the same chiral emitter‐based CPL photodetectors exhibit a high photocurrent anisotropy factor ( g ph ) of 0.3 and sustain stable performance over 1000 switching cycles. This work establishes a versatile approach for developing chiral hybrids, unlocking their potential for multifunctional integrated chiral optoelectronics.

title: High-Performance Chemiresistive Humidity Sensing and Quantum Isotopic Differentiation with Single Crystals of a Conductive MOF Hosting Electron Spin Qubits
abstract: Conductive metal–organic frameworks (MOFs) offer a versatile platform for chemiresistive humidity sensing, a capability vital for industrial and biomedical applications. However, grain boundaries and uncontrolled crystallite orientations in commonly used polycrystalline devices limit sensing performance, while electrical responses alone lack specificity for distinguishing H2O from D2O. Here, we report high-performance chemiresistive humidity sensing and quantum isotopic differentiation using single crystals of a representative conductive MOF, Cd2(TTFTB) (TTFTB4− = tetrathiafulvalene tetrabenzoate). Leveraging intrinsic charge transport modulated by a solvent screening effect, the single-crystal devices significantly outperform polycrystalline counterparts that exhibit negligible sensing capability. Specifically, they achieve an ultralow detection limit of 100 ppm, a broad dynamic range up to 100% relative humidity, and a high average on/off response exceeding 3 × 106. Comparative measurements across solvent vapors reveal selectivity for water vapor and relate current modulation to solvent dielectric constant, hydrogen-bonding ability, and molecular volume. Furthermore, we harnessed the electron spin coherence of embedded TTF⋅+ radical qubits in a collection of Cd2(TTFTB) crystals to unambiguously distinguish H2O from D2O via hyperfine spectroscopy, complementing high-performance single-crystal chemiresistive detection with quantum-enabled isotopic identification. Taken together, these results demonstrate the feasibility and considerable promise of a dual-mode sensing approach that integrates chemiresistive and quantum sensing.

title: Thermally Induced Structural Transformation in a Two-Dimensional Conductive Metal-Organic Framework
abstract: A long-standing structural question in triphenylene-based conductive metal-organic frameworks is why closely related materials adopt either fully extended honeycomb lattices or intercalated structures containing alternating extended layers and discrete metal–ligand clusters. Ni(II)–HHTP and Co(II)–HHTP (HHTP = 2,3,6,7,10,11-hexahydroxytriphenylene) have both been reported to have the latter “intercalated structure”, but here we discover that thermal activation and dehydration convert both frameworks to the fully extended structures. Focusing on Ni(II)–HHTP, we show that this structural transformation is reversible, with roomtemperature hydration restoring the intercalated structure. Variable-temperature synchrotron powder X-ray diffraction supports the intercalated-to-fully-extended structural transformation, while solid-state nuclear magnetic resonance spectroscopy, thermal analysis, and elemental analysis provide evidence for the accompanying dehydration. Rehydration of Ni(II)–HHTP restores the intercalated structure, establishing reversible structural switching through removal and reincorporation of water. The resulting change in interlayer architecture alters electrical conductivity, gas response and adsorption properties in Ni(II)–HHTP. Importantly, common sample pre-treatment and testing conditions can themselves change the type of framework structure, meaning that measured properties may not correspond to the initially assigned structure. Because thermal and hydration history determine structure and function, careful structural verification under measurement conditions is, therefore, essential for establishing reliable structure–property relationships. Ultimately our findings resolve a persistent structural ambiguity in this family of materials and allow access to new fully extended electrically conductive framework materials.

title: Organic Iron Sulfur Framework With Electron Transfer Capacity Promotes Photosynthetic Carbon Fixation
abstract: ABSTRACT Iron‐sulfur clusters (ISCs) are crucial prosthetic groups in natural proteins that participate in vital electron transfer processes. Although various artificial ISCs with catalytic activity have been constructed, synthesizing stable ISCs under aerobic conditions remains a significant challenge. Here, we report a hydrothermal synthesis strategy to produce metal–organic frameworks (MOFs) containing discrete ISCs, bridging the gap between biological ISCs and conventional iron sulfide minerals. Using terephthalic acid (TPA) as the organic linker to encapsulate ISCs, we constructed MOF‐like nanosheets termed Organic Iron‐Sulfur Frameworks (OISF). Comprehensive characterization, including Mössbauer spectroscopy have confirmed the crystal structure of OISF containing [2Fe‐2S] cores. The OISF exhibits robust electron transfer capability toward various acceptors, mediated by the dynamic formation of interlayer S─S bonds. Leveraging this property, OISF is combined with chloroplasts to enhance dark reactions in vitro and applied as a fertilizer to promote the growth of spinach in vivo, highlighting the potential of stable ISCs in biochemical and industrial applications.

title: Framework desymmetrization enables partial pore space partition in metal-organic frameworks
abstract: Abstract The pore-space-partition (PSP) has been recognized as a powerful strategy for boosting the uptake capacity of small gas molecules and has seen wide application in reticular chemistry. However, the most successful PSP platform—the partitioned- acs (pacs) net—has followed only one pattern since its inception over a decade ago: one partition agent per partition site, with a general formula of [M 3 O( L1 ) 3 ]( L2 ). This fully partitioned architecture occupies all metal sites, eliminating open metal sites (OMSs) and compromising selectivity. Herein, we introduce a partial PSP concept accessed through a framework desymmetrization strategy. By replacing traditional high-symmetry D 2h ligands with lower-symmetry C 2h ligands (e.g., fumaric acid), we introduce structural distortions into the acs network, breaking the uniformity of partition sites and allowing partition agents to occupy only a fraction of available positions. This provides access to a PSP mechanism, namely part-pacs (partially partitioned- acs ), with a general formula of [M 3 O( L1 ) 3 ]( L2 ) 1/3 . The part-pacs structures retain high acetylene capacity while exhibiting significantly enhanced selectivity compared to their fully partitioned analogues. Specifically, part-pacs-fum-tpa achieves C 2 H 2 /CO 2 separation productivity nearly twice that of its full-pacs counterpart (1.92 mol kg −1 vs 0.98 mol kg −1 ).

title: Position‐Resolved Fluorescence Polarization Maps Segmental Rigidity in Block Copolymer Micelles in Aqueous and Biological Media
abstract: ABSTRACT Polymeric micelles are widely used as nanoscale compartments for delivery, sensing, and soft‐matter applications, yet their performance is governed not only by size and morphology but also by the local mobility of polymer segments within the assembly. Here, we describe a position‐resolved fluorescence polarization strategy to map apparent segmental rigidity within block copolymer micelles. By covalently installing the same dansyl fluorophore at defined positions along an amphiphilic block copolymer chain, we selectively label the hydrophobic core, core‐corona interface, and oligo(ethylene glycol) (OEG)‐rich corona of the micelles. The resulting fluorescence polarization profiles reveal a pronounced core‐to‐corona apparent rigidity gradient in water, distinguish block‐segregated micelles from compositionally matched random copolymer assemblies, and report micellar responses to temperature, cosolvent, and salt. This method further enables structural interrogation of polymer micelles in biologically relevant media, revealing the unexpected finding that biological serum exerts opposing effects on apparent chain rigidity in the micellar core and corona. Together, these results establish position‐resolved fluorescence polarization as a practical platform for linking block copolymer structure, self‐assembly, local chain dynamics, and biological stability, opening new opportunities to rationally design micelles with environment‐responsive mechanical properties.

title: Modulation of low-molecular-weight cellulose self-assembly using a nonionic amphiphilic block copolymer
abstract: Abstract Artificial nanocelluloses constructed through the self-assembly of low-molecular-weight (LMW) cellulose have emerged as sustainable nanomaterials with tailorable nanomorphologies. Herein, we demonstrate the modulation of LMW cellulose self-assembly using Poloxamer 407 (P407), a poly(ethylene oxide)—poly(propylene oxide)—poly(ethylene oxide) triblock copolymer. LMW cellulose with average degrees of polymerization of approximately 7 and 10 formed nanosheets or nanoribbons in the presence of 15% and 20% (w/v) P407, while their dimensions and aggregation states varied markedly depending on the conditions. In particular, the former LMW cellulose formed nanosheets in intimate contact with one another with poorly defined boundaries at 15% (w/v) P407, while nanosheets with irregular, stepped edges were formed at 20% (w/v) P407. Fourier transform infrared spectroscopy and matrix-assisted laser desorption/ionization time-of-flight mass spectrometry analyses suggested that P407 directly interacted with LMW cellulose and affected its self-assembly. These findings reveal that amphiphilic block copolymers can serve as effective modulators of LMW cellulose self-assembly and expand strategies for controlling the nanomorphologies of artificial nanocelluloses without chemical modification of cellulose molecules.

title: Electrochemically Engineered Gold Nanostructures for Selective Detection of Glucose and Ascorbic Acid
abstract: This study reports the development and characterization of modified screen-printed carbon electrodes (SPCE) for the non-enzymatic simultaneous detection of glucose and ascorbic acid. The electrodes were modified with gold nanoparticles (AuNPs) using a cyclic voltammetry electrodeposition process. The morphological and topographical evolution of the AuNPs layer was systematically investigated for 5, 10, and 15 deposition cycles using scanning electron microscopy and confocal microscopy. The key contribution of this work lies in correlating the electrodeposition-driven morphological evolution of gold nanostructures with analyte-specific oxidation behavior and electrochemical signal discrimination under mutual interference conditions. The electrochemical performance of the SPCE/15AuNPs electrode was evaluated showing an enhanced electrochemically active surface area of 1.154 mm². The optimized platform demonstrated excellent electrocatalytic activity towards the oxidation of glucose and ascorbic acid in individual and mixed solutions. Analytical validation in a 0.1 M NaOH/PBS matrix showed that the sensor maintains high selectivity and sensitivity even in the presence of significant interference. For glucose detection in a 10 mM ascorbic acid background, the sensor exhibited a linear range of 0.1–10 mM with a sensitivity of 0.03 mA/mM and a limit of detection (LOD) of 1.46 mM. Conversely, for ascorbic acid detection in a 10 mM glucose background, a linear response was obtained from 0.1 to 7 mM with a sensitivity of 0.02 mA/mM and an LOD of 1.02 mM. Interference studies with urea, sucrose, and histidine further confirmed the robust selectivity of the hierarchical AuNP surface. These results suggest that the developed SPCE/15AuNPs electrode is a promising, low-cost tool for multi-analyte sensing in complex biological fluids.

title: Influence of the Geographical Origin on Properties and Chiral Nematic Self-Assembly of Carboxylated Cellulose Nanocrystals from Degreased Cotton
abstract: Abstract The intrinsic properties of cellulose are influenced by the geographical origin of its raw material, which in turn significantly affect the characteristics of cellulose nanocrystals (CNCs) derived from organic acid hydrolysis and consequently their chiral self-assembly behavior. In this study, carboxylated cellulose nanocrystals (C-CNCs) were prepared from degreased cotton sourced from six different regions in China via oxalic acid hydrolysis. The influence of geographical origin on the physicochemical properties of the resulting C-CNCs and their chiral nematic self-assembly behavior was systematically investigated. The results revealed that variations were observed among the six C-CNC samples in aspect ratio, carboxyl group content, and Zeta potential. Samples with higher aspect ratios and more negative zeta potentials could develop well-defined chiral nematic liquid crystalline fingerprint textures. And the second critical concentration (C 2 ) for complete anisotropy decreased with the increasing aspect ratio, while the helical pitch at C 2 increased with both aspect ratio and carboxyl content. Alkaline pretreatment was adopted to pretreat the samples that failed to form chiral nematic phases, aiming to enhance I β content, crystallinity, and hydroxy-group accessibility by disrupting the hydrogen-bonding network. The resulting N-CNCs exhibited smaller dimensions, higher aspect ratios, and more negative zeta potentials, successfully self-assembling into chiral nematic phases with fingerprint textures and iridescent films.

title: Self-Assembly of a Carboxyl -Bipyridinium Zwitterion into a High-Performance Photoswitchable NLO Crystal
abstract: Abstract Efficient photoswitchable second-order nonlinear optical (NLO) materials are highly attractive for optical signal processing. However, achieving high-performance switching in molecular crystals remains challenging, requiring simultaneous optimization of response speed (&lt;120 s saturation), modulation depth (∼90%), and operational durability. Here, we report an asymmetric, purely organic carboxylate-bipyridinium salt crystal that satisfies these criteria: peak ON/OFF NLO contrast high up to 95%, saturation within 120 s, and stable cyclability. Upon irradiation, intramolecular electron transfer generates carboxylate-bipyridinium radicals that are molecularly localized yet electronically coupled through cofacial π−π stacking along extended columns. This radical−π coupling broadens visible absorption and enables efficient, reversible switching. The synergy between structurally permitted photoinduced electron transfer and intermolecular radical coupling establishes a design principle for organic photonic switches combining rapid response with high contrast.

title: Self-Assembled Nanomaterial-Based Wound Dressings for Cutaneous Wound Healing: A Structured Narrative Review
abstract: Self-assembled nanomaterial-based wound dressings are emerging platforms for cutaneous wound repair. These materials have been reported to provide antimicrobial activity, antibiofilm effects, hemostatic support, wound monitoring, and tissue-regenerative functions. This structured narrative review summarizes primary studies evaluating self-assembled or self-assembling nanoscale materials for cutaneous wound applications. A structured PubMed search was conducted on 9 June 2026 using predefined Boolean terms and PubMed filters for Free full text, English, Humans, and Other Animals. Eligible studies assessed a dressing, scaffold, hydrogel, film, patch, bandage, or topical biomaterial containing at least one nanoscale component and reported at least one wound-related outcome. Reviews, non-cutaneous wound studies, inaccessible full texts, and studies limited to synthesis or characterization without wound-related testing were excluded. The unfiltered search retrieved 367 records; after filters, 67 records were screened, and 23 primary studies were included. Five broad material groups were represented: self-assembling peptide systems, supramolecular small-molecule systems, polymer/polysaccharide/protein-based systems, nanocellulose-based systems, and hybrid nanocomposites. Most studies were preclinical: 17 combined in vitro testing with animal models, four were limited to in vitro or ex vivo models, and two were animal-only in vivo studies. No human clinical studies meeting the eligibility criteria were identified among the included studies. Overall, self-assembly provides a flexible design principle for multifunctional wound dressings, but the current evidence remains predominantly preclinical and requires further translational validation.

title: Host–Guest Inclusion Self-Assembly of Zero-Dimensional Metal Halides for Enhanced Photocatalytic Amine Coupling
abstract: Abstract The practical application of zero-dimensional (0D) organic–inorganic hybrid metal halides in photocatalysis is hindered by their poor stability, rapid charge-carrier recombination, and low surface reactivity. Herein, we report a host–guest self-assembly strategy for constructing two 0D anionic metal halides with enhanced photocatalytic activity, [(L1)2⊂(ZnCl4)2–3] (C1) and [(L1)2⊂(MnCl4)2–3] (C2), by one-pot reaction of an anthracene-pyridine-based cationic cavity ligand (L13+·3Br–) with ZnCl2 and MnCl2·4H2O, respectively. Single-crystal X-ray diffraction reveals that both compounds feature discrete tetrahedral [MX4]2– cores yet exhibit distinct lattice packing modes; notably, in C1, the anionic cluster is anchored via C–H···Cl hydrogen bonds rather than direct encapsulation. The host–guest inclusion systems of discrete metal halides exhibit optical band gaps of 2.19–2.27 eV, with observable charge separation. Under 455 nm blue-light irradiation, C2 demonstrates exceptional photocatalytic performance in benzylamine coupling (TOF of 492.66 h–1), achieving 71–99% conversion across 10 substrates and about 90% activity retention after five cycles, while C1 shows lower activity (TOF of 463.58 h–1). EPR spectroscopy and quenching experiments uncover a radical-based synergistic mechanism. These results show that host–guest self-assembly affords stable 0D metal halide photocatalysts and that metal-center exchange significantly affects catalytic activity.
